source: Supplied revised report, sections 1 and 2; paragraph text preserved.
status: Design specification; acceptance criteria have not been runtime-tested.

stories.title: Create Animal Intake Record
stories.story: AS A Shelter Staff Member, I WANT to record complete intake information, SO THAT I identify each animal throughout shelter care.

criteria.text: Require species, approximate age, sex, coat markings, arrival circumstances and intake timestamp before completing intake.
Capture arrival source and surrenderer contact details or transferring officer name, council and contact details, as applicable.
For council transfers, require paperwork attachments or an explicit not applicable reason before assessments are enabled.
Generate a unique shelterId; reject duplicate identifiers without creating another animal record.
Require at least one identification photograph linked to the intake record before completion.
Completed intake sets Under Assessment and enables independent health, ownership and behaviour assessments.

stories.title: Assess Animal Health and Manage Treatment
stories.story: AS A Veterinarian, I WANT to document examination and treatment decisions, SO THAT I establish medical fitness before public adoption.

criteria.text: Save animal reference, examinedAt, veterinarian, body condition, dental health, coat and skin condition, and injury findings.
Record species-specific screening results; document blood or faecal samples as collected, pending, negative, positive or not required.
Require urgentTreatmentRequired Boolean; true means the veterinarian judges delay risks immediate deterioration, with urgentTreatmentReason recorded.
Urgent cases require treatmentPlan and immediate-care recording; unresolved treatment blocks clearance and public listing.
Record dated treatment, monitoring, treatmentOutcome and reassessment findings in the same MedicalRecord linked to the animal.
Only a veterinarian can clear the urgent flag after reassessment; recovery returns the animal to combined fitness review.

stories.title: Determine Ownership and Behavioural Suitability
stories.story: AS A Shelter Staff Member, I WANT to record ownership and temperament outcomes, SO THAT I prevent unlawful or unsuitable public listing.

criteria.text: Record microchip detection; require microchipNumber when detected and retain the registry lookup outcome.
For identified owners, store contact attempts, holdJurisdiction and holdUntil using the applicable statutory period.
Before holdUntil, block clearance; verified reclamation records return to owner and closes the intake without listing.
Record responses to handling, animals, food and unfamiliar people, with assessor, assessment date and suitabilityResult.
An unsuitable result requires behaviour referral and reassessment; permanent unsuitability closes the public-adoption pathway.
Combined fitness review requires three completed assessments; listing additionally requires ownership clear, suitable behaviour and medical fitness.

stories.title: Prepare Animal for Public Adoption
stories.story: AS A Veterinarian, I WANT to complete preparation and authorise clearance, SO THAT I make eligible animals available for adoption.

criteria.text: Record species-appropriate vaccination type, administration date and boosterDueDate; reject missing or chronologically inconsistent dates.
Record desexingStatus as completed or scheduled; a scheduled procedure requires a date and identified shelter policy permitting listing.
Vaccination and desexing preparation proceed independently; both must satisfy policy before medical clearance.
Clearance records veterinarian and sign-off time; unresolved treatment, ownership hold or unsuitable temperament blocks authorisation.
Only cleared animals can change from Under Assessment to Available for Adoption; failed transitions retain the previous status.
Publish approved photographs, temperament notes and medical summary only; owner, applicant and raw clinical records remain private.

stories.title: Assess Adoption Application
stories.story: AS A Shelter Staff Member, I WANT to assess each complete adoption application, SO THAT I select suitable applicants for a meet-and-greet.

criteria.text: Require selected available animal, applicant contact, household, referee and adoption-reason details; missing fields prevent completed submission.
Assign applicationId and preserve submissions; incomplete applications return for correction before suitability review.
Record referenceCheckResult, contacted referee, date and supporting evidence; pending results cannot support approval.
Record homeSuitabilityResult, tenure, yard security and landlord permission; not applicable decisions require a reason.
Record petCompatibilityResult and species or temperament evidence; no existing pets is recorded explicitly with justification.
All three satisfactory results permit progression; any unsatisfactory result requires rejection reason, applicant notification and available status restoration.

stories.title: Finalise Adoption Placement
stories.story: AS A Shelter Staff Member, I WANT to confirm compatibility and placement prerequisites, SO THAT I finalise a valid adoption.

criteria.text: Schedule a meet-and-greet only after approval; store application reference, meetingAt and supervising staff.
Record compatible or incompatible outcome with observations; an unrecorded outcome blocks finalisation.
Incompatibility closes that application, records notification and restores the animal to Available for Adoption.
Compatibility enables signed agreement and payment confirmation in parallel, linked to the same application.
Require signature reference and successful payment reference; missing, failed or pending payment blocks finalisation.
Finalisation creates one AdoptionRecord and sets Adopted before the final medical check; duplicate requests cannot create duplicate placements.

stories.title: Complete Final Medical Release and Follow-Up
stories.story: AS A Veterinarian, I WANT to confirm fitness and care requirements before release, SO THAT I support safe placement and follow-up.

criteria.text: Record the final examination date, veterinarian and latestMedicalCheckPassed against the adopted animal.
Record applicable care instructions, medication schedule and dietary advice; identify not applicable items explicitly.
A failed check sets Release Paused; treatment and a new examination are required before release can resume.
Release remains blocked until the latest check passes, regardless of an earlier clearance or successful payment.
Staff confirm recipient and releasedAt only for a valid adoption with a passed current check.
After release, require followUpMethod and followUpDueAt within the agreement period; retain completion outcome when follow-up occurs.

stories.title: Protect Role-Based Access
stories.story: AS A Shelter Staff Member, I WANT to use authenticated role permissions, SO THAT I prevent unauthorised changes.

criteria.text: Each staff account has a unique identifier; passwords use salted one-way hashing and never appear in logs.
Staff manage intake and placement; veterinarians authorise clinical outcomes; applicants access only their own applications.
Direct unauthorised requests return no protected data and log actor, action, timestamp and denial outcome.
Five failed logins in 15 minutes lock the account for 15 minutes or until authorised administrator unlock.
Internal sessions expire after 15 inactive minutes; the next protected request requires authentication.
Permission changes take effect within five minutes, including existing sessions, and record administrator and timestamp.

stories.title: Preserve Personal and Sensitive Data Privacy
stories.story: AS A Prospective Adopter, I WANT to protect my personal and household information, SO THAT I apply without unnecessary privacy exposure.

criteria.text: Use TLS 1.2 or later in transit and encrypted databases and backups; reject unencrypted protected-data requests.
Public responses and exports exclude owner contacts, microchip numbers, applications, payment details and raw medical notes.
Before application submission, display collection purpose and record privacy-notice version, acknowledgement and timestamp.
Veterinarians access release contacts and care needs; household and referee evidence remains staff-restricted.
Store payment reference and outcome only; never store card verification codes or full payment-card numbers.
Apply a management-approved retention schedule; delete or irreversibly de-identify expired personal data within 30 days, logging completion.

stories.title: Maintain Responsive Performance
stories.story: AS A Shelter Staff Member, I WANT to receive prompt system responses, SO THAT I complete time-sensitive shelter work.

criteria.text: Animal-search response time is at most two seconds at the 95th percentile with 50 active internal users.
Public listings become usable within three seconds at the 95th percentile with 100 concurrent visitors.
Valid intake, assessment and status updates confirm within two seconds at the 95th percentile.
A valid 10 MB photograph uploads and confirms within five seconds at the 95th percentile.
Valid application submission confirms within three seconds; retrying the same request returns the same applicationId.
A 30-minute mixed-load test uses 50 internal users, 100 visitors and 10,000 animals; server errors remain below 1%.

stories.title: Sustain Availability and Recoverability
stories.story: AS A Shelter Staff Member, I WANT to retain dependable access and recovery, SO THAT I continue animal care after system failures.

criteria.text: Achieve 99.5% monthly availability, measured by successful one-minute probes, excluding approved announced maintenance.
Announce maintenance 48 hours ahead; schedule outside the proposed 08:00 to 18:00 shelter operating window.
Three consecutive failed probes trigger an alert to support within five minutes of the first failure.
Back up critical records every 15 minutes and take encrypted daily backups stored separately from production.
Recovery loses at most 15 minutes of committed data and restores critical service within four hours.
Quarterly restoration verifies identifiers, relationships and latest committed values across animal, medical, application, agreement and placement records.

stories.title: Support Usable and Error-Resistant Work
stories.story: AS A Shelter Staff Member, I WANT to use clear consistent workflows, SO THAT I avoid welfare and placement errors.

criteria.text: After 60 minutes of training, each participant completes intake within five minutes without critical error.
Required fields are identified before submission; validation identifies the field, problem and corrective action.
Validation failures preserve all valid entries and attachments; users correct errors without re-entering unaffected information.
Rejection, adoption finalisation and release require a confirmation showing animal, application, previous status and proposed outcome.
Status labels match the domain model across forms, searches, dashboards and exports.
Five representative staff perform four core tasks each; at least 18 of 20 succeed unaided, with zero unsafe releases.

stories.title: Preserve Record Integrity and Auditability
stories.story: AS A Shelter Staff Member, I WANT to retain consistent traceable records, SO THAT I trust welfare and placement decisions.

criteria.text: Intake and adoption finalisation commit all required related records atomically; injected failure leaves no partial transaction.
Unique constraints reject duplicate shelterId and applicationId; repeated finalisation returns the existing adoption record.
Updates include record version; stale submissions are rejected with a conflict message and retain unsaved user changes.
Critical changes log actor, UTC timestamp, record identifier, action and before-and-after values.
Ordinary users cannot change or delete audit entries; retention follows the approved audit schedule.
Daily checks report orphan records, invalid status transitions and released animals without passed checks within one hour; affected finalisation is blocked.

stories.title: Provide Accessible Public Services
stories.story: AS A Prospective Adopter, I WANT to use accessible public listings and forms, SO THAT I browse and apply independently.

criteria.text: All public browse-and-apply pages satisfy WCAG 2.2 Level AA, checked manually and with automated tools (W3C, 2024).
Every interaction works by keyboard, with logical focus order, visible unobscured focus and no keyboard trap.
Controls expose accessible names; screen readers announce required fields, validation errors and submission outcomes.
Meaningful animal photographs have descriptive alternative text; decorative images are ignored by assistive technology.
Text contrast meets 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text; 200% zoom preserves all content and functions.
Test current and previous Chrome, Edge and Safari releases, plus NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari.
